annotations.title: Tenor Melody Projection & Whispering Arpeggios
annotations.instruction: Liszt marks the melody to be played by the right-hand thumb and shared with the left hand in the tenor range. Keep the surrounding six-eight broken chords completely sotto voce while projecting the cantabile line with warm arm weight.

annotations.title: Cadenza I: Weightless Pearly Touch
annotations.instruction: Do not stiffen the wrists. Keep fingers curved and light as feathers (leggierissimo), letting momentum carry the chromatic double-arpeggio cascade upwards and downwards.

pedalGuidance.explanation: Use soft pedal (una corda) and hold damper gently to blend the harmonic overtone aura without clouding.

annotations.title: Appassionato Assai: Full Orchestral Resonance
annotations.instruction: Deliver triumphant fortissimo octaves in both hands. Use your back and shoulders for power rather than isolated finger tension, creating an impassioned, resonant romantic swell.

pedalGuidance.explanation: Clear pedal crisply on the principal downbeats to prevent acoustic muddiness during dense chord changes.

annotations.title: Cadenza II: Pearly Descending Arabesque
annotations.instruction: After the thunderous climax, dissolve into crystalline pianissimo drops. Decelerate gracefully into the return of the main theme in A-flat major.

annotations.title: Nocturnal Coda: Timeless Stillness
annotations.instruction: Allow the final low A-flat pedal points to ring freely. The arpeggiated chords should sound as though suspended in mid-air, fading into complete serenity.

pedalGuidance.explanation: Hold the damper pedal throughout the final two bars until the acoustic vibration naturally dissipates.
